findings.where: Hero at phone width: the order of the photograph, Mark's line, the yellow 'Write to me directly' strip and the paragraph 'I advise multilateral development banks…'
findings.fault: On the phone, the photograph and the big line fill the first screen. The yellow address strip lands right at the fold, and the only sentence saying what Mark does and for whom comes after the strip, below the first screen. So the visitor is asked to write before being told what he advises on. The strip is meant as the foot of the sheet, but here it sits in the middle of the frame with the explanation hanging under it.
findings.who_objects: An official at a development bank opening the link on a phone from LinkedIn or email. On the first screen they see a face and an opinion about PPPs, but nothing saying he advises banks like theirs. They have to scroll past the contact strip to find out, so the 5-second test fails on the device where they are most likely to glance and leave.

findings.where: Navigation (Profile · Articles · Blog) and the end of the page
findings.fault: The navigation has no Contact item, and the page ends without a footer giving the address. The hero's yellow strip is the only way to reach Mark. Once the visitor scrolls past it, or lands on an article or profile page, nothing in the structure shows them how to get in touch.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who has read his work and decided to write. Getting in touch is the site's one action, and for a solo advisor the house's first-visit trust rule asks for the address on every page and a Contact label in the navigation. Without them, this visitor has to go back to the homepage hero.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the end of the article and the 'Download' row ('Streamlining the PPP Process…', Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF)
findings.fault: The article ends on a bare 'Download' label linking to a different lecture, so it is unclear whether this is the article's own PDF or something unrelated. The 'PDF' label suggests a direct file download rather than a page for the talk. There is also no author line with his World Bank credential and no way to write to him at the point where the article has persuaded the reader. The byline gives only his name.
findings.who_objects: A reader who reached the article from a shared link and never saw the homepage. They don't learn who Mark is (the house's rule on identity for deep pages), they can't tell what they are downloading, and at the moment they are most convinced there is no way to contact him.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the headline 'The World's Best' and the closing paragraph 'the world's best PPP law'
findings.fault: Both apostrophes are straight typewriter ticks, while the quotation marks and the captions ('Mark's photo') use curly ones. At display size in the headline, the tick stands out against the refined serif.
findings.who_objects: A reader who expects the polish of a legal journal, and the founder judging a direction built on 'editorial gravitas'. A straight tick in the largest line of the article page looks careless.

findings.where: Article page specimen at desktop: the 'Download' row
findings.fault: The date and format ('Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF') are pushed to the far right edge of the column, apart from the two-line title they describe. They read as a separate item rather than as the title's details.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning for the newest talk and its date. They have to look across an empty gap to connect the date with the title. When more items are added, the dates will read as a column of their own.

findings.where: Hero header: the lockup of the aqueduct mark, 'MMM INFRA' and 'Mark M. Moseley'
findings.fault: The heavy dark arches of the logo come first and carry more visual weight than his name, which sits after them at a modest size. So the firm's mark leads and his name comes second, the reverse of 'his name leads, with the logo beside it'.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose personal-advisor test says Mark's name leads and the firm does not. A visitor's eye goes to the portrait, the line, the address and then the logo before it reaches his name.
